revise.summary: I revised content/lessons/07-spec-and-issues.md and fixed every finding: 1 high, 16 mediums and 23 lows. Both gates pass: the lint prints no ERROR lines (2,813 words) and vitest ran 14 tests, all passing. The structural fix moves the destination-and-route paragraph and the big-idea callout under "The idea" heading, so "Why it matters" now ends on why the decisions must go into files and defines `/implement` there. The Try now covers permission prompts, explains plan mode and grilling rounds, gives a sample reply for the seam check, and replaces "read the .scratch folder" with asking the agent to list the files and show spec.md. In the questions, why-destination-route is replaced by a new scenario-near-smart-zone (the /compact exception), and spot-horizontal, spot-seam-skip, scenario-wide-rename, scenario-too-many-tickets, first-tracer-bullet and why-write-it-down were reworded to remove giveaways and weak distractors. The Site story now holds only what the repo shows (old Lessons 03 and 11 at d21fc2c, the ticket files under .scratch/lesson-site and .scratch/main-flow-and-redesign, the PR #9 body). The words "the seam" are replaced by the repo's own "one design choice", plus a fact about the Skill. One deviation from the brief: it said the M6mYodf0dJM transcript is not on this machine, but an English auto-caption file exists at /Users/siddharth/Developer/trying/.handoff/transcripts/M6mYodf0dJM.en.json. I used it, together with the -QFHIoCo-Ko and hX7yG1KVYhI caption files, only to check the existing paraphrases (46.1k tokens, three slices cut to one, tickets.md, 11 tickets, "too horizontal", six tickets merged to four, look harder, day shift). Nothing new is quoted from M6.

reader.where: Opening promise, line 11: "turn your grilling into a spec (where you're going) and a set of tracer-bullet tickets (how you'll get there), before you clear anything"
reader.problem: The first sentence a cold Visitor reads has five terms nobody has explained yet: session, grilling, spec, tracer-bullet tickets, clear. "Tracer-bullet" is explained 99 lines later (line 110), session at line 24, spec and ticket at line 42. Other Lessons' promises use plain words.
reader.evidence: Lesson line 11. Writing guide, Voice: "Explain every term at or before first use, in a clause". Pilot review: "Define Claude Code, agent, Skill, token, session, repo, spec, ticket ... at first use". Compare 04-grilling.md:11 "Before an agent writes a single line of code, let it interview you until you both want the same thing." and 08-tdd.md:11, both jargon-free.
reader.fix: When a build is too big for one sitting with your coding agent, write what you agreed into a spec (one document saying where you're going) and a few thin tickets (small tasks that get you there), before you wipe the conversation.

reader.where: Why it matters, line 26 ("do that in two steps, `/to-spec` and `/to-tickets`") and Checkpoint why-write-it-down, lines 30, 34, 36
reader.problem: The Checkpoint's options use "spec file", "ticket" and "tracker" before the Lesson explains them. Spec and ticket are first explained at line 42 and the issue tracker at line 48. Line 26 introduces `/to-spec` and `/to-tickets` without saying what a spec or a ticket is, so a cold reader meets the Checkpoint without the words it uses.
reader.evidence: Line 30: "until a spec file exists". Line 34: "The tracker deletes old conversations after each session." Line 36: "copies the whole conversation into each ticket". Definitions come only at line 42 ("`/to-spec` writes a ==spec==: one document...") and line 48 ("It asks which issue tracker you use: the place a project keeps its tasks").
reader.fix: Line 26: "Matt's Skills (...) do that in two steps: `/to-spec` writes a spec (one document saying what to build and why), then `/to-tickets` cuts it into tickets (small tasks, one session each), picking up where his grilling Skill, `/grill-with-docs`, left off." Line 34: "- [ ] Claude Code deletes each conversation when the session ends." with feedback "  > It doesn't delete it. The problem is that a new session starts without the conversation in its context window." To stay in budget, shorten line 42 to the parts that are new (destination and route, and that the spec outlives the tickets).

reader.where: /to-spec section, line 88: "and `/code-review` checks the finished code against the spec"; also Final test spot-seam-skip feedback, line 362: "what `/code-review` checks against"
reader.problem: Typing `/code-review` starts Claude Code's own Built-in command of that name, which is a bug hunt and does not check against the spec. A reader who takes the backticked name literally would run the wrong thing. The Lessons on TDD and Implement both warn about this clash; this Lesson doesn't.
reader.evidence: writing-guide.md, Facts: "Claude Code has its own Built-in `/code-review` ... Matt's Skill is always reachable as `/mattpocock-skills:code-review`." 08-tdd.md:209: "(Type `/mattpocock-skills:code-review` for Matt's: Claude Code ships its own `/code-review`, a Built-in command with the same name.)" 09-implement.md:125 says the same.
reader.fix: Line 88: "Later, `/tdd` (...) writes tests only at seams you agreed, and Matt's `code-review` Skill checks the finished code against the spec (type `/mattpocock-skills:code-review` to start it yourself; plain `/code-review` reaches Claude Code's Built-in command of the same name)." Line 362: "  > Seams decide where `/tdd` writes tests and what Matt's `code-review` checks against. They're yours to agree, not the agent's to guess."

reader.where: Try it yourself, step 7, line 249: "Confirm the summary, then type `/to-spec`."
reader.problem: The grilling Skill holds off acting only until you confirm. After a bare "yes", the agent may start building the to-do page. Step 3 has just told the reader to choose Yes whenever it asks to create files in todo-practice, so a beginner would approve the build and then run `/to-spec` on an app that already exists. The step also doesn't say that `/to-spec` must start a new message. Line 57 makes that the rule, and a beginner is likely to type "Yes, that's right. /to-spec" as one message.
reader.evidence: skills/engineering/grilling/SKILL.md:30: "Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding." 04-grilling.md:253 guards against the build: "end with: \"Don't build anything.\" If it starts creating files anyway, press Esc". Lesson line 57: "by typing the name at the start of your message".
reader.fix: 7. Confirm the summary and add: "Don't build anything yet." (If it starts creating files anyway, press Esc.) Then, in a new message, type `/to-spec`. When it stops to show you the seams, reply before typing anything else: "Yes, that matches", or, if it proposes several, ask whether one would do.

reader.where: Common mistakes, line 265: "**Clearing or compacting before `/to-tickets`.** One window for grilling, spec and tickets."
reader.problem: This contradicts the Lesson's own exception and its own Final test. Line 186 says to `/compact` at a phase boundary when the session nears the end of the Smart zone before `/to-tickets`. The right answer of scenario-near-smart-zone (line 399) is to compact before `/to-spec`. Common mistakes lists that same move as a mistake, with no exception.
reader.evidence: Line 186: "The one exception: if the session nears the end of the Smart zone before `/to-tickets`, `/compact` at the nearest phase boundary". Line 399: "- [x] `/compact` now, at the end of grilling, then type `/to-spec`." ask-matt/SKILL.md:40: "If a session approaches it before `/to-tickets`, don't push on degraded; `/compact` at the nearest phase boundary and carry on".
reader.fix: - **Clearing before `/to-tickets`, or compacting while there's still room.** One window for grilling, spec and tickets; `/compact` only if you near the end of the Smart zone first.

reader.where: Why it matters, line 24 ("A feature this size won't fit in the room you have left"), with the same test at line 26, the table at line 182 and the Cheat sheet at line 286
reader.problem: The Lesson's main decision (goal 1, and the first Final test question) is whether the work "fits the room this session has left". It never tells a cold reader how to see that room, so they can't make the decision. The grilling Lesson gives the one-line answer.
reader.evidence: Line 182: "Decided, and it fits the room this session has left | `/implement`, right here". Line 286: "Grilling done, fits this session | `/implement`, right here". 04-grilling.md:186: "Type `/context` to see how full yours is." Nowhere in 07-spec-and-issues.md mentions `/context`.
reader.fix: After "...as a rule of thumb." on line 24, add: "Type `/context`, a Built-in command (one that comes with Claude Code itself), to see how full yours is." Then shorten the later gloss to "Clear the window instead with `/clear`, another Built-in command, and the agent starts again with none of the conversation."

reader.where: Site story, line 272: "length limits on comments, rejecting unknown Slugs, and deploying the empty app early"
reader.problem: "Slugs" is a glossary term this Lesson never explains. A cold reader can't tell what "rejecting unknown Slugs" means.
reader.evidence: grep finds "Slug" only at line 272 of 07-spec-and-issues.md. GLOSSARY.md: "**Slug**: A Lesson's permanent one-word identifier (e.g. `grilling`)."
reader.fix: ...length limits on comments, rejecting unknown Slugs (a Slug is the permanent one-word name in a Lesson's web address, like `grilling`), and deploying the empty app early.

accuracy.where: ## `/to-tickets`: tracer bullets with blocking edges, "acceptance criteria: checks that prove it's done, so each must be able to fail" (line 125)
accuracy.problem: The sentence sits in a list of what the Skill writes into each published file, so it reads as if the Skill makes sure every acceptance criterion can fail. It doesn't. Matt's docs name criteria that grade nothing as a known, recurring failure, and they say you have to check this yourself. The Lesson never tells the Visitor to check it, and its 'It's working if' list only asks for 'a checklist'.
accuracy.evidence: ~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/docs/engineering/to-tickets.md:76-77: "The acceptance criteria graded nothing: some passed before any work was done." / "The template asks for criteria and says nothing about whether they can fail, so this happens." It goes on to say the check is worth doing by hand. skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md:79-80: the template has only "- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1 / 2", with no rule that a criterion must be able to fail.
accuracy.fix: Replace the end of the sentence with: "... `Status: ready-for-agent` and acceptance criteria: checks that prove it's done. The template doesn't make sure each one can fail, so read them: a criterion that's already true before any work starts proves nothing."

accuracy.where: ## The idea: a destination and a route, "points to it from `CLAUDE.md` ... (or from `AGENTS.md`, if the repo already has that)" (line 48)
accuracy.problem: The rule is slightly off. Setup uses AGENTS.md only when there is no CLAUDE.md. If a repo has both, it edits CLAUDE.md. If it has neither, it asks which one to create. As written, a reader with both files could expect AGENTS.md to win. The [Skills](/learn/skills) Lesson gets this right: "With no `CLAUDE.md` it uses `AGENTS.md`".
accuracy.evidence: skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills/SKILL.md:76-78: "If `CLAUDE.md` exists, edit it. / Else if `AGENTS.md` exists, edit it. / If neither exists, ask the user which one to create". content/lessons/03-skills.md:165.
accuracy.fix: "... and points to it from `CLAUDE.md`, the file of standing instructions the agent reads at the start of every session (or from `AGENTS.md`, if the repo has that and no `CLAUDE.md`; with neither, it asks which to create)."

accuracy.where: ## Try it yourself, It's working if: "The tickets are separate files, `01-…`, `02-…`" and "there are two or three, not ten" (lines 258, 260)
accuracy.problem: For a tiny to-do page, a correct run can end with a single ticket. Step 8 tells the Visitor to merge any ticket that has nothing to demo, and Matt's own run went from three slices to one. A Visitor who gets one good ticket would wrongly mark two checks as failed.
accuracy.evidence: Lesson line 250 (step 8): "Merge any ticket without a good answer, then approve." skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md:52-56: the Skill asks whether the size is right and should anything merge, and iterates until the user approves. M6mYodf0dJM transcript 12:39-12:53: "three slices ... I actually think it can be done in one slice" (also in the Lesson, line 211).
accuracy.fix: "- [ ] Each ticket is its own file (`01-…`, then `02-…` if there's more than one), with **What to build**, **Blocked by**, `Status: ready-for-agent` and a checklist." and "- [ ] Each ticket delivers something you could try in the browser, and there are one to three, not ten."

accuracy.where: ## The idea: a destination and a route, "The spec stays as the record of why; each ticket is done with once it's built." (line 42)
accuracy.problem: This holds while the tickets are being built. But the same docs say the spec is a snapshot that goes stale, to be treated as disposable once the work ships, and that GLOSSARY.md and the ADRs are the files meant to last. A cold reader could treat the spec as a lasting record.
accuracy.evidence: docs/engineering/to-spec.md:45: "the spec stays as the one place that records the reasoning behind them". docs/engineering/to-spec.md:54: "Treat it as disposable after the work ships. Your `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs are the files meant to last."
accuracy.fix: "The spec keeps the why while the tickets are built; each ticket is done with once it's built. After the work ships, `GLOSSARY.md` and the ADRs are what last."

accuracy.where: ## How Matt and others use it, "counted 17 `/implement` runs in which `/tdd` never ran, and traced it to tickets dropping the seams" (line 218)
accuracy.problem: The Lesson overstates the issue. It hedges: the data comes from one user's sessions, and the pattern is only called "consistent with" the leak.
accuracy.evidence: gh issue view 1078 --repo mattpocock/skills: "Observed in one user's local corpus (1125 sessions, so a single-user sample): 17 `/implement` runs, 0 `/tdd` invocations" and "The pattern is consistent with the leak". State: OPEN.
accuracy.fix: "A September 2026 GitHub issue found 17 `/implement` runs in one user's sessions where `/tdd` never ran, and linked it to tickets dropping the seams `/to-spec` agreed. It's still open, which is why you check the seam yourself."

accuracy.where: ## How Matt and others use it, "rebuilt a karting-tracker app with the Skills in October 2026" (line 217)
accuracy.problem: The post is dated October 2026, but it never says when the rebuild happened. It only says he heard the podcast that prompted it "last month". The date belongs to the write-up, not the rebuild.
accuracy.evidence: https://blog.scottlogic.com/2026/10/19/an-honest-review-of-matt-pococks-skills.html, dated 19 October 2026: "Last month I listened to Gergely Orosz ... interview Matt Pocock" and "I decided to rebuild the app from scratch". No date is given for the rebuild. The other details check out: CTO at Scott Logic, one seam proposed, eight tickets, and a data model preferred over user stories for CRUD.

quiz.where: Common mistakes, "**Clearing or compacting before `/to-tickets`.** One window for grilling, spec and tickets." (line 265), against Final test scenario-near-smart-zone, keyed answer "`/compact` now, at the end of grilling, then type `/to-spec`." (line 399)

They are then pushed to b ("Push on"), the only option that neither clears nor compacts. Only the body (line 186) gives the Smart zone exception that the answer key depends on.
quiz.evidence: Lesson line 186: "The one exception: if the session nears the end of the Smart zone before `/to-tickets`, `/compact` at the nearest phase boundary". quiz.where: Final test, scenario-wide-rename, options at lines 311-317 ("Add the new name beside the old, migrate in batches, then delete the old." vs "One tracer-bullet ticket…", "One ticket that renames…", "One ticket per layer…")
quiz.problem: Wording tell: all three wrong options start "One … ticket". Only the right option starts with a verb, and it restates the body's three steps almost word for word (lines 131-133), so the odd one out wins. A sharp reader could also argue for c: the stem never says the rename is too big for one session, and c's feedback rests on "no green point along the way", even though a single pass that lands is green. The real reason, taught at line 117, is that a ticket must fit one fresh context window.
quiz.evidence: Lesson lines 311-317 and 117 ("It fits in one fresh context window"). to-tickets/SKILL.md:33: "Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window". to-tickets/SKILL.md:40 (wide refactor: "a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once"). writing-guide.md:62 ("no wording tells").
quiz.fix: Stem: "Your team has to rename a field used in about 3,000 places, far more than one session can change. Renaming it anywhere breaks every caller still using the old name. How should the tickets be shaped?" Right option: "- [x] One ticket adding the new name, one per batch of callers, then one deleting the old." (84 characters; d stays 85, so the right answer isn't the longest). Option c: "- [ ] One ticket that renames all 3,000 places in a single pass." with feedback "  > 3,000 call sites won't fit in one fresh context window, and nothing is green until the last one changes."

quiz.where: Final test, scenario-too-many-tickets, stem "a change that fits easily in this session" (line 334) and right option "Push back now: merge them, or skip tickets and `/implement`." (line 337)
quiz.problem: The right option is the most hedged: it joins two moves with "or", so a reader can choose it as the catch-all. Its own feedback says such a change "needs no tickets at all", so the "merge them" half is the weaker move. The stem also mixes two traps: it puts single-session work into `/to-tickets` without saying so, then tests ticket size.
quiz.evidence: Lesson line 338: "a change that fits one session needs no tickets at all". writing-guide.md:62 ("One unambiguous right answer… no wording tells").
quiz.fix: Stem: "A blog's sharing feature needs several sessions. In `/to-tickets`' breakdown, the "copy link" button alone is nine tickets: one for the icon, one for the click handler, one for the "Copied!" message, and so on. What's your best move?" Right option: "- [x] Say they're too fine, and merge the button into one ticket." with feedback "  > Right. The review step is where you fix the size. One button is one demoable slice, and every extra ticket costs a fresh session's start-up." Keep a, c and d.

quiz.where: Final test, spot-seam-skip, stem "While `/to-spec` was waiting for an answer about which seams to test at, Sam typed `/to-tickets` to keep things moving." (line 358)
quiz.problem: The stem gives away the mistake. It says the Skill was waiting for an answer and Sam typed something else, so the right option ("Sam never agreed the seams…") can be read straight off the stem. The scenario is also the Site story's own slip and the body's highlighted rule retold, so it tests recall rather than whether the reader would recognise a seam check in a fresh session.
quiz.evidence: Lesson line 276: "I typed `/to-tickets` instead of answering, so the spec got written with the agent's best guess." Line 88: "==Answer the seam question before you type anything else.==" writing-guide.md:118: "Don't restate the defining phrase of the right answer in the prompt."
quiz.fix: Stem: "Sam ran `/to-spec` for a shop's refunds feature. It explored the code and ended its message: "I'd test at the existing orders module and a new refunds module. Does that match what you expect?" Sam typed `/to-tickets` to keep things moving. Spot the mistake." Keep the options and feedback.

quiz.where: Checkpoint first-tracer-bullet, options at lines 139-144 ("every page of the finished design", "Recipes, ratings and comments can all be stored", "recipes, ratings and comments through the API")
quiz.problem: Every distractor is wide, and the right option ("one recipe") is the only narrow one. A reader can pick it by "choose the one that says one" without knowing that a tracer bullet must also cross every layer.
